question: Does consolidating queried evidence through known-family posterior prediction improve durable acquisition, and does it expose an advantage from informative query selection?
old_replay: Stage1 exactly two of eight examples per batch resampled from stage0 queried device0 observations in every condition. No additional queries.
posterior: Uniform prior over the declared 88-rule family; Bernoulli observation noise 0.1; hard posterior predictive majority labels using only the queried input/observed-bit ledger. Ties select zero.
training_inputs: Observed condition cycles over its own query ledger; posterior condition uniformly shuffles the acquisition split without replacement. Equal device exposures and token counts. Unqueried hidden labels are unavailable to the builder.
primary_endpoint: Clean-context forced-choice single-device accuracy after stage1, final checkpoint only.
contrasts: oracle minus random within each consolidation condition
posterior minus observed within each acquisition condition

screen_qualification.claim: Prespecified seed29 factorial screen: known-family acquisition and inference-consolidation upper bounds, not a learned general active agent. Positive effects need fresh-seed confirmation.

uncertainty: Paired bootstrap by device and causal input bits0..4; describes example sampling only, not training-seed uncertainty.
limits: Known-family oracle privileges apply to selection and posterior inference separately.
Heldout single-device examples introduce new nuisance-bit combinations, not new causal truth-table states.
No test-driven checkpoint or hyperparameter selection.
